question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(3{n}^{2}-1)(3{n}^{2}+1)}{{n}^{2}(4-9{n}^{3})}=\frac{9{n}^{4}-1}{4{n}^{2}-9{n}^{5}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{9{n}^{4}-1}{4{n}^{2}-9{n}^{5}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $-9{n}^{5},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{9{n}^{4}-1}{4{n}^{2}-9{n}^{5}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9{n}^{4}}{{n}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{n}^{5}})}{(\frac{4{n}^{2}}{{n}^{5}}-\frac{9{n}^{5}}{{n}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9}{n}-\frac{1}{{n}^{5}})}{(\frac{4}{{n}^{3}}-9)} \\  & =\frac{0-0}{0-9} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $0.$
